articles.title_orig: Trump and Xi dined with AI's biggest names. Here's what we know about tech talks so far
articles.title_zh: Trump and Xi dined with AI's biggest names. Here's what we know about tech talks so far
articles.content_orig:
This report is from this week's The Tech Download newsletter. Like what you see? You can subscribe here.
It's the morning after the night before, as the U.S. President Donald Trump hosted Chinese President Xi Jinping in a historic state dinner. Fricassée, sea bass and crémeux were all on the menu, as presumably, was a whole lot of chatter about AI.
Seated with the U.S. and Chinese presidential couples were Nvidia's Jensen Huang and his wife Lori Huang, SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and AMD's Lisa Su, as well as Apple's Tim Cook. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and president Greg Brockman, Google cofounder Sergey Brin and Microsoft boss Satya Nadella were also all on the guest list.
Warnings around the existential risks of AI reaching fever pitch in recent weeks have pushed AI to the top of the global geopolitical agenda.
Trump posted to Truth Social ahead of his and Xi's head-to-head.
"Super Intelligence (SI) will be a big topic of discussion, but I want to leave it exactly where it is. That is China's position also," he wrote Thursday morning, using the term he recently adopted instead of AI.
So what did they actually discuss?
A Chinese readout of the meeting said President Xi pointed out that China and the U.S. "may have competition, but they may cooperate even more " in AI.
"The two sides can continue their dialogue on AI, exchange views on its risks and benefits, and jointly prevent the misuse and abuse of AI," Xi said, per the readout. "AI must be kept under human control. A people-centered approach should be upheld, and AI should be developed for the positive and for good, so that AI will serve the progress of humanity."
Trump, the Chinese readout stated, said the two sides should "maintain dialogue and strengthen cooperation on AI." The U.S. government had not issued its own readout of the summit as we went live.
Those references to cooperation come after U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent discussed a "U.S.-China AI dialogue" with his Chinese counterpart, He Lifeng, over the weekend, including a channel for incidents "up to a national security level."
That has been compared to the Cold War era "red phone" — a direct channel between the U.S. and Russia designed to prevent a nuclear crisis escalating.
Both U.S. and Chinese administrations had already shot down the idea of guardrails or a slowdown in developing the tech, which Altman and Anthropic's Dario Amodei had called for, alongside a number of their companies' researchers.
While more details about the meeting are expected to be released in the days to come, specifics are scant so far.
"It appears we ended up with an intent to continue dialogue, along with a hotline of some sort for emergencies," Aalok Mehta, director of the Wadhwani AI Center at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, told CNBC.
While the China camp's post-meeting readout sounds friendly, there were a number of flashpoints that could've made for a tense conversation.
U.S. export controls that restrict China's ability to import advanced Nvidia chips were set to remain a sticking point.
Though, as CNBC reported on Wednesday, recent new chip releases and AI models from Chinese tech giants sharpen Beijing's case that Washington's restrictions have their limits.
Friction could also have come from Chinese companies' reported remote access to Nvidia chips, via overseas data centers, and American claims of "distillation."
Time will tell if any progress was made on those issues. And if it was, there's no guarantee if either side will reveal any specific commitments.
But ongoing discussions could lead to agreements around AI with more substance, said Mehta.
"The hotline itself could become a robust tool when paired with a proper incident reporting system. But that will take real commitment to making it work and high-level engagement from both sides."
An OpenAI agent gained unauthorized access to an Australian government website, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said , raising fresh questions about the risks posed by increasingly autonomous systems.
Anthropic and OpenAI on Tuesday each announced new, less costly AI models as both frontier labs continue to face stiff competition from cheaper, open-weight competitors.
AMD stock surged 10% on Monday, pushing shares to a record high and topping a $1 trillion market cap benchmark for the first time.
Qualcomm unveiled its newest Android phone chipsets, which will be tuned for on-device AI and will compete with Apple's A20 Pro in iPhones.
OpenAI on Monday posted a set of proposals for AI safety with a heavy focus on alignment research and a computing technique known as recursive self-improvement, or RSI.
And lastly, we leave you with a hot take from an esteemed colleague. Senior tech correspondent Arjun Kharpal had this to say on Meta's Muse agent:
Meta's Muse is more of a challenge to Google than OpenAI and Anthropic.
The consumer AI market is still up for grabs and the biggest players are going to be those that can produce a useful agent, the type that companies have promised. Plus, they'll need to earn the trust of users, especially as we have had all of these cybersecurity incidents recently.
Google has all the ingredients to have done this first — control of a mobile operating system in Android, search dominance, a plethora of apps from email to maps. All of that should have allowed it to create a useful agent with Gemini that could potentially be powerful on Android devices, which make up the majority of the world's smartphones.
But Meta has beaten it to the punch.
That's not to say Google is down and out, but Meta has certainly laid down the gauntlet. To some extent, Meta is also challenging Apple to come up with something strong with Siri to ensure the Cupertino giant can leverage its massive install base of iOS users.

articles.title_orig: Sen. Duckworth slams Trump's "foolhardy plan" to make triumphal arch a military complex
articles.title_zh: Sen. Duckworth slams Trump's "foolhardy plan" to make triumphal arch a military complex
articles.content_orig:
Democratic Sen. Tammy Duckworth of Illinois is demanding the Pentagon and Federal Aviation Administration reject President Trump's call to convert plans for a massive triumphal arch into a "top grade Military Complex" equipped with snipers and with the capability to store, launch and land drones while in the flight path of Washington's Ronald Reagan National Airport.
"The FAA and DoD must reject this foolhardy plan and instead focus on increasing the safety of the airspace," Duckworth, who lost both legs while serving in the Iraq War, wrote in a letter to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford.
The FAA determined last week that the 250-foot arch, which is being constructed near Arlington National Cemetery, poses no hazard to flights coming into and departing from Reagan Airport.
The letter was exclusively obtained by CBS News. She called Mr. Trump's announcement, made in a Truth Social post over the weekend, "bizarre, unhinged early morning social media rants."
In the letter sent Friday, Duckworth, the ranking Democrat on the Senate Subcommittee on Aviation, Space, and Innovation, took Trump administration officials to task for "wasting time, energy and taxpayer dollars on yet another Trump vanity project."
She called it "particularly outrageous" after what she described as the "joint failure" of the FAA and Defense Department "to effectively implement corrective actions that were recommended" by the NTSB following the January 2025 midair collision near Reagan Airport that killed 67 people.
The NTSB made 52 safety recommendations following the collision between a U.S. Army Black Hawk helicopter and an American Airlines regional jet that was landing at Reagan Airport.
Thirty-five recommendations were directed to the FAA, only three of which have been closed. The NTSB said earlier this month the FAA's responses to 11 of the recommendations were unacceptable. All 13 recommendations directed at the Pentagon remain open.
"It is disturbing to see Federal officials devote enormous attention to an unnecessary, proposed structure while the NTSB and the public are still demanding action on recommendations intended to prevent another catastrophic collision in our skies," Duckworth wrote. "The American people cannot afford to stand witness to Trump's risky plan to place a 250-foot structure along a busy approach path, especially if he follows through on plans to station snipers on the arch and fly drones ... in the already congested airspace."
While calling the FAA's review of the proposed arch "incomplete," Duckworth, a former Army helicopter pilot, is demanding answers to a host of questions, including if the FAA considered the use of the arch as a military complex during its safety assessment.
She is also calling for Hegseth to disclose "which military entity, if any, requested that the arch be converted into a 'Military Complex,' and what threat assessment supports that request?"
She requested answers by Oct. 5.
In a statement earlier this week, Democratic Rep. Don Beyer of Virginia wrote that "putting a drone launching site directly in the landing path for DCA is a stupid, dangerous, and unworkable idea."
The FAA and Defense Department declined to comment on the arch, referring inquiries   to the White House.
Eleanor  Watson contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Pope Leo XIV begins historic 4-day visit to France
articles.title_zh: Pope Leo XIV begins historic 4-day visit to France
articles.content_orig:
Pope Leo arrived in France on Friday, Sept. 25, starting a four-day tour across Paris, Lourdes, and Metz that includes speeches and a massive outdoor mass. (HOST BROADCASTER via Reuters.)
Pope Leo XIV began his visit to France on Friday for his fifth Apostolic Journey as Pontiff. The four-day trip marks the first formal papal visit to the country once called "the eldest daughter of the Church" since Pope Benedict XVI’s visit in September 2008.
French bishops announced the visit’s theme as "That the world may have life," and it comes as the officially secular nation is seeing an influx of new baptisms. So far this year, according to the Conference of Bishops of France, more than 21,000 adults have joined the Church, an increase driven by 18 to 25-year-olds.
"Pope Leo's visit to France has sparked a real tidal wave" of interest, retired French Bishop Marc Stenger told Reuters. "French Catholics are… saying ​loudly that they need the Church to find their way in these uncertain moments in world history."
POPE LEO WARNS AI RISKS BECOMING TOOL OF 'DOMINATION, EXCLUSION AND DEATH' IN NEW ENCYCLICAL
The pope will visit Metz on Sept. 28, 2026 to conclude his four-day state and pastoral trip to France, which also includes stops in Paris and Lourdes. (Jean-Christophe Verhaegen / AFP via Getty Images)
The rise comes after a 2021 report found that some 330,000 French children had been abused by Catholic clergy and lay leaders over seven decades, and said the Church had shown "deep, total and even cruel indifference" ​to victims. Stenger, who led the Diocese of Troyes from 1999 to 2020, told Reuters the scandals "have deeply wounded the Church and damaged its credibility."
In what is described as an unusual move, the Vatican press office announced Pope Leo will meet privately in Lourdes with seven of those victims as part of a message of healing and vulnerability.
SAN FRANCISCO ARCHDIOCESE AGREES TO $395M SETTLEMENT WITH 530 CLERGY ABUSE SURVIVORS
The Vatican calls the trip, "a journey that unites faith and public engagement, memory and the future, with listening and bridge-building at its heart." After being greeted by French President Emmanuel Macron and a courtesy visit to Élysée Palace on Friday, Pope Leo is scheduled to make 15 speeches during his visit. He is expected to speak on several spiritual and societal themes, including the need to protect immigrants , the sick and unborn, and defend human dignity in the era of AI, and address themes of peace, culture, and unity.
President of France Emmanuel Macron and First Lady Brigitte Macron welcome Pope Leo XIV to Élysée Palace on Sept. 25, 2026 in Paris, France. (Tom Nicholson/Getty Images)
French bishops have expressed surprise at the level of interest in the visit. The Associated Press reports organizers for Pope Leo’s Saturday Mass at Paris’ Place de la Concorde, expecting up to 1 million people, have lengthened the security perimeter, extending the site beyond the 1.2-mile length of the Champs-Élysées, where Pope Leo will parade in the Popemobile.
Among his more noteworthy stops, Pope Leo will worship and speak on Sunday at the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Lourdes, one of Christianity’s most-visited pilgrimage destinations, especially popular with the sick. It is where an ailing Pope John Paul II , on his final foreign trip in 2004, delivered a forceful condemnation of abortion and euthanasia.
Pope Leo XIV attends the Welcome Ceremony at Paris Orly International Airport on Sept. 25, 2026 in Paris, France. (Simone Risoluti - Vatican Media via Vatican Pool/Getty Images)
Pope Leo’s visit, however, comes after France’s recent national debate and subsequent passage of legislation allowing adults with incurable illnesses to receive lethal medication. That followed 2024 legislation enshrining abortion as a constitutional right .
POPE LEO PROMOTES ARCHBISHOP WHO BARRED PELOSI FROM COMMUNION TO ONE OF VATICAN'S HIGHEST COURTS
On Friday, Pope Leo will speak at the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization, or UNESCO, headquarters in Paris. Vatican spokesman Matteo Bruni says Leo will likely reiterate his call for an AI slowdown and speak "with regard to the meaning of existence, to what makes human beings human and what does not."
The speech comes after the Pope’s May manifesto in which Leo warned of the dangers of AI and urged international regulation of the industry. His position again puts him at odds with President Trump, who has encouraged AI innovation so the U.S. can compete with and surpass China.
A crucifix stands in front of the Basilique Notre-Dame du Rosaire, its spire draped with a banner marking the upcoming visit of Pope Leo XIV, five days ahead of the pontiff's trip to the site as part of his apostolic journey to France, in Lourdes on Sept. 22, 2026.
Following his UNESCO visit, Pope Leo holds a prayer service at the newly-restored Cathedral of Notre-Dame, marking the first papal visit since a 2019 fire nearly destroyed one of France’s national landmarks.
He concludes his trip on Monday with a symbolic full-day visit to the border city of Metz, the birthplace of former French Prime Minister Robert Schuman, considered one of the founding fathers of the European Union. It is a backdrop the Vatican says the Pope will use to "champion friendship among European peoples."

French Ambassador to the Vatican Charles Personnaz told Reuters that Macron has invited leaders from all 27 EU members to attend the speech and meet with the Pontiff. Other media reports say Ukrainian President V olodymyr Zelenskyy may also attend.
Reuters and The Associated Press contributed to this report.
Tyler Speicher is an American journalist living in Slovenia after spending 25 years covering stories ranging from the Little League World Series to hurricanes, 9/11 and its aftermath for New York City news outlets, including 20 years on the Fox News Channel assignment desk.

By BETHAN EDWARDS, SHOWBUSINESS REPORTER
Published: 05:28 EDT, 25 September 2026 | Updated: 05:41 EDT, 25 September 2026
Taylor Swift appeared to issue an apology to an ex-boyfriend in her new single Pink Clouding as she sang: 'I left scars on a good person - you didn't deserve it.'
The billionaire popstar, 36, dropped four new songs Patient Zero, Cleveland! Pink Clouding and Babylon on Friday, as an extended edition of her 2025 album The Life of a Showgirl.
And in The Encore's third new track Pink Clouding, it appears to not be about Taylor's husband Travis Kelce but instead sounds like it's about an ex-boyfriend who she didn't want to let down so ended things.
'Pink clouding', sometimes called Pink Cloud Syndrome, describes a period of intense optimism or euphoria that can occur early in addiction recovery before the realities and difficulties of recovery set back in.
The expression can also be used more broadly to describe a temporary euphoric state or the feeling that everything is suddenly rosy.
In the chorus, she sings: 'Cause I was pink clouding from the thrill of it (Pink) / Skydiving as you wrapped your arms around my body / Gray rocking where the arrow hit (Gray) / Years later, I still wonder how to tell you sorry / I didn't want to let you down (Pink cloud, pink cloud) / So I left you up there on a pink cloud (Pink, pink cloud).'
Taylor Swift appeared to issue an apology to an ex-boyfriend in her new single Pink Clouding as she sang 'I left scars on a good person - you didn't deserve it'
Fans speculated that Taylor was singing about ex Tom Hiddleston, who she dated in 2016 (pictured), as she sang that she didn't want to let him down so ended things
Taylor seems to apologize to this ex on the bridge, she sings: 'I hope / You realized my kind of trouble wasn't worth it / And the way I treated you, you never deserved it / And I swear to God, to this day / I wake up scared that I left scars on a good person / And I gave you zero reason to believe it / So be it / But it didn't mean nothing /Just 'cause I could leave it'
At the end of the song Taylor, who is famed for documenting her romantic woes through her music, says she hopes this guy 'landed safely on the ground' and 'I hope you're so happy now.'
It is unknown which of Taylor's exes the song is about but many fans speculated online that it could be about Tom Hiddleston who she dated in 2016.
The actor, who dated the hitmaker for just three months, famously wore an 'I heart T.S' T-shirt during a fourth of July party they threw with friends.
He told GQ magazine at the time: 'The truth is, it was the Fourth of July and a public holiday and we were playing a game and I slipped and hurt my back and I wanted to protect the graze from the sun and said, ‘Does anyone have a T-shirt?’ And one of her friends said, ‘I’ve got this’ … And we all laughed about it. It was a joke.'
Tom added that he was not a fan of the limelight which comes with being in such a closely scrutinised relationship.
Last year the Loki star welcomed his second child with his fiancée, actress Zawe Ashton.
Taylor later moved on with Joe Alwyn, who she dated from 2017 until 2023.
However some also speculated the track was about Harry Styles, who is going to be marrying Taylor's good friend Zoe Kravitz. They previously dated in late 2012 to early 2013.
Fans wrote on X: 'Is pink clouding about tom hiddleston………..;
'Patient Zero is about Matty Healy and Pink Clouding about Joe Alwyn. She literally just said he was so good and didn’t deserve the way she treated him, that she wants to apologize;
'Not to paternity test (sorry Taylor) but Pink Clouding has Tom Hiddleston written alllll over it;
'If I say that Pink Cloud is for Harry, are you guys gonna call me crazy?'
Some fans also speculated the track was about Harry Styles, who is going to be marrying Taylor's good friend Zoe Kravitz. They previously dated in late 2012 to early 2013
Fans wrote on X: 'Is pink clouding about tom hiddleston………..; If I say that Pink Cloud is for Harry, are you guys gonna call me crazy?'
Fans seemed to enjoy the new track though with many calling it  a 'true masterpiece' while one added, 'oh taylor pink clouding should've been the single... THIS HAS ME MOVING.'
Another penned: 'Pink Clouding is giving 1989 omg I'm gonna cry,' referring to Swift's 2014 album.
'Hear me out is she referring to a like one night stand type thing?' an X user questioned, and account Taylor Nation commented, '"So I left you up there... On a pink cloud"... please give us 1-3 business days to recover.'
Meanwhile fans are convinced that new single Patient Zero – a single about a toxic former relationship – is about her romance with Joe Alwyn .
The couple dated for six years from 2017 until early 2023, in what was Taylor's longest, and arguably most low-key, relationship to date. There were rumours of an engagement, but neither Joe nor Taylor publicly confirmed the reports.
Now fans believe she's documented their romance in Patient Zero which saw Taylor seemingly sing about a social-climbing ex.
The single has similarities to her 2022 track, You’re Losing Me – widely believed to be about Joe – which referenced medical terminology, while Patient Zero has a pulse sound in the background.
You're Losing Me has the lyrics 'Stop (Stop, stop), you’re losing me / I can’t find a pulse, my heart won’t start anymore,' which echo Patient Zero's 'When the toxins take their hold / You’d rather die than let it go.'
Patient Zero also has similarities to another track believed to be about Joe – 2019's Cruel Summer – in which she referred to him as 'grinnin’ like a devil'.
In Patient Zero, she sings about 'the devil on his shoulder under his halo'.
Other lyrics from her new single reference an ex stepping into the spotlight after dating her – with English actor Joe relatively unknown outside the UK before their romance.

She sings: 'I bet he burst into your life like fireworks/I bet he even said "I love you" first/And when you saw another woman coming out of his place/I bet he kissed the rain off your face.
'I know he charmed your family and friends/And you thought it's 'cause he loves you/But it's 'cause he loves how everybody loves him.
'I know it seems like he shines bright/But he's bathing in your reflected light/On a free social climb.'
The music video for Patient Zero stars Irish actor Colin Farrell, with actress Dakota Johnson, with Ireland having links to her Joe relationship because the couple stayed in Dublin while Joe filmed the series, Conversations With Friends.
They are also said to have spent £50,000 renting Glin Castle in County Limerick for a romantic Christmas getaway over six days in 2018.
Taking to X/Twitter after the single's release, fans speculated the single is about Joe, who is now rumoured to be dating Love Story actress, Sarah Pidgeon.

'Taylor calling Joe Alwyn a devil disguised as an angel, an emotional parasite who uses women's shine to climb socially. And yet she presents herself as patient zero, the first victim of that disease. Patient zero got emotional';

articles.title_orig: Russia could attack a NATO country within months, Danish intelligence warns
articles.title_zh: Russia could attack a NATO country within months, Danish intelligence warns
articles.content_orig:
Danish intelligence officials have warned that Russia could launch a "limited" military attack against a NATO member in the coming months, saying the Kremlin appears more willing to take risks after more than four-and-a-half years of war against Ukraine.
The Danish Defence Intelligence Service (DDIS) on Thursday identified a "low but growing risk" that Russia could carry out isolated strikes with long-range weapons on infrastructure that is critical to the support of Ukraine.
"A limited military attack would be a desperate move on Russia's part and, like the intensified hybrid attacks, could potentially take place in the coming months," it wrote in a report.
"The purpose would be to redirect European resources away from supporting Ukraine and to sow division within NATO, should the alliance fail to agree on a collective response."
The DDIS added that it saw no indications that Russia would launch an outright invasion of a NATO country, although it said it could not rule this out.
Russia could also deploy a limited number of troops, possibly without national insignia, into NATO countries on its border, DDIS said. However, it said that such a build-up would be difficult to conceal and take several months to prepare.
The new threat assessment joins a chorus of Russia warnings from top European security officials and lawmakers in recent days.
NATO members that border Russia include Finland, Norway and Poland, as well as the Baltic states of Latvia, Estonia and Lithuania.
Poland's government on Thursday said a blaze at a Starlink ground station in the country was an act of sabotage aimed at disrupting internet services, including for Ukraine's military.
Poland's deputy prime minister, Krzysztof Gawkowski, said it had not yet been established who was responsible for the fire, but "many signs suggest this aligns with Russia's new ‌doctrine ⁠of attack," according to Reuters .
A spokesperson for Russia's Embassy in London was not immediately available to comment when contacted by CNBC. The Kremlin has previously denied involvement in similar incidents.
Denmark's intelligence also warned that Russia will intensify its hybrid war by carrying out more attacks against the West and NATO, "with greater consequences for the targeted countries than in the past."
These could include major cyberattacks that seriously damage vital societal functions as well as sabotage attacks with a high risk of casualties, DDIS said.

articles.content_orig:
An early-season nor'easter will bring coastal flooding, high surf, strong winds and rain to parts of the East Coast through the weekend, with impacts from North Carolina to New England.
New York City and especially Boston need to stay weather aware this weekend, and prepare the same as you would for a tropical storm.
The nor'easter is strengthening as it heads north. The map below shows the winds and rain as the low moves north along the East Coast.
Wind gusts over 30 mph, with occasional gusts from 40 to 50 mph, are occurring along the coast from southeast New England to the Outer Banks of North Carolina.

Dolan added: "We can only interpret, therefore, that he supports the content of the book. And that means he supports an attack on his father, the man he's trying to build bridges with."

Although the sun in Libra usually encourages clear and balanced thinking, Neptune’s influence could interfere today. You might find yourself caught in an echo chamber: You’ll hear what you want to hear and ignore the rest, and you’ll believe the stories that confirm your biases rather than the ones that are actually true. The best way to avoid major problems is to recognize that your judgment might be temporarily suspect — and put off important decisions for a day or two. Clarity will come, but you have to be willing to wait for it.
While some people seem to enjoy being coy and playing games, you prefer to be straightforward; you don’t see the point in making people guess at your feelings. But today, without even realizing it, you’ll give off some confusing signals. You might think you’re being crystal clear, but others might not understand what you’re asking for. You might assume you’re leaving little room for doubt, but don’t underestimate other people’s capacity for misinterpretation. Make a point of being as unambiguous as possible right now, even at the risk of overexplaining yourself.
Most days, you trust your intuition to steer you right, especially when there are no obvious right answers and you have to make a judgment call. Sometimes no amount of logic or analysis can tell you what to do; you simply have to go with your gut. But other times what feels like intuition is really just your anxiety talking — or your personal biases disguised as simple “gut feelings.” You needn’t ignore your impulses entirely today, but be aware of instances when you might need to balance your instincts with outside opinions and ordinary common sense.
You’ll quickly lose your way today if you try to please everyone. You already know this deep down, but still — it’s easy to forget. Making everyone happy can seem like a productive and rewarding use of your time; being liked feels good! But your challenge right now is to hold tight to your principles, even if you fear they’ll make you unpopular. It might be difficult in the moment, but your future self will be grateful that you stood firm.
Today, the things that draw the most praise and attention from people around you might take you by surprise. Others might seem focused on achievements that you think are no big deal; the qualities you consider most ordinary in yourself will enrapture everyone else. You might imagine that they’re just flattering you or that they’re misguided, giving you accolades you don’t deserve. But consider, too, that perhaps they’re the ones accurately assessing your skills — and you’re the one giving yourself too little credit.
You sometimes find trying new things stressful; you worry about the inevitable mistakes you’ll make in the beginning. When you’re exploring new places, you always seem to wander before you’ve gotten your bearings; when you’re learning new skills, your first attempts are often clumsy. Part of you will probably always hope you’ll be a natural, able to skip over the awkward beginner stages entirely. But trial and error is an important part of personal growth. Today, make sure that you don’t let your fear of making mistakes prevent you from branching out.
The people you thought you could count on might turn out to be surprisingly unreliable today. You might find that friends who once promised they’d do “anything” for you might suddenly find excuses if you ask for a favor. That doesn’t necessarily mean you should write them off completely, especially if they’re usually dependable. But pay attention to patterns. If someone makes big promises but then always seems to disappear when you need them, it might be time to revise your opinion of them.
You tend to take for granted that you and your friends share many of the same values and opinions. You know each other well enough that you can guess what the other is thinking — and most of the time, you’re right. But today, unless you’ve explicitly discussed things, don’t be so sure that you’re automatically in alignment. There’s far too much potential for miscommunication right now: You’re likely to make some unfounded assumptions about your friends’ feelings and intentions, and they’re likely to do the same. So take the extra time to explain your thinking and ask questions about theirs before you make any sudden moves today.
You don’t think of yourself as particularly sensitive. In fact, your goal is to be as tough and resilient as possible, able to bounce back from anything. But there’s only so much stress you can absorb before it will start to wear you down. Problems that would be minor annoyances on a good day can feel like the last straw on a difficult one. Today, you might be more thin-skinned than usual — not because you’ve suddenly become “fragile” or “weak,” but because you’re dealing with a lot lately. Cut yourself some slack.
Sometimes, your thrillingly unconventional and counterintuitive ideas end up being the best ones — the ones that fix your biggest problems and change the world around you. But there are also times when offbeat ideas are just … bad . Remember that, in plenty of cases, the obvious, run-of-the-mill solutions are the best ones. It can be hard to see this clearly when you’re longing for excitement, but today, don’t let your hunger for novelty and drama cause you to lose your good judgment.
You might assume that the people who’ve known you the longest are the ones who also know you best . They’ve seen you through all your different phases, in good moments and bad — so you tend to take their advice more seriously. But today, remember that they’re not infallible. Listen to their input, but if it doesn’t ring true, don’t hesitate to choose a different path. They might have valuable perspectives to offer, but they don’t know everything. You are still the one who knows yourself best.
You might feel less mentally sharp today. Don’t be surprised if you make mistakes you ordinarily never would. You might mix up details, forget names, or accidentally let important tasks slip through the cracks. No matter how smart and capable you usually are, things sometimes get muddled. Try not to panic: The problem isn’t that there’s something wrong with you but that you’re trying to keep track of too much at once. Stop expecting yourself to manage everything single-handedly, and start asking for some help.
You try to see the best in people, but today it might be wise to keep your guard up — at least for now. If you’re not careful, you’ll be quick to trust people with charming exteriors but bad intentions, or to give credence to stories that are too good to be true. The problem isn’t that you can’t see the red flags, but that part of you would rather not. You want so badly to believe that wonderful things are possible, and they are! But remember that you also have strong critical thinking skills. Use them.

Investigators concluded the sexually charged remark constituted sexual harassment and said Caldwell's denial that he made the comment was not credible.
The staffer said she subsequently attempted to distance herself from Caldwell at work and avoid traveling with him when possible.

New Jersey Lt. Gov. Dale Caldwell was called on to resign by Gov. Mikie Sherrill after an independent investigation substantiated sexual harassment and ethics violations. (Tim Larsen via New Jersey Governor’s Office)
"I’m calling for his resignation and giving him until tomorrow to do so," Sherrill said Thursday, calling the substantiated sexual harassment finding "extremely troubling."
The report also substantiated two ethics violations, finding Caldwell brought personal guests to ticketed events without advance ethics clearance or payment and repeatedly attempted to secure a promotion for a state employee with whom he had a romantic relationship.
Investigators found Caldwell continued bringing unpaid guests to events despite repeated training and warnings, including on May 23, one day after he was formally notified of the investigation.

Fox News Digital reached out to Caldwell for comment on the report and Sherrill's resignation demand .

"The lieutenant governor’s resignation is necessary and in the best interest of New Jersey residents," the Democrat said.

articles.title_orig: Benjamin Netanyahu attacks Israel’s enemies and allies in UN speech
articles.title_zh: Benjamin Netanyahu attacks Israel’s enemies and allies in UN speech
articles.content_orig:
Delegates walk out of Netanyahu’s UN speech
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has used his platform at the United Nations General Assembly to attack detractors and allies alike, and his presence sparked uproar in the chamber.
Speaking before the UNGA on Thursday, Netanyahu attacked New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, critics and Iran’s leadership, as well as allied countries like the United Kingdom, Turkiye and France.
Back home, the prime minister is locked in a tight race to stay in power ahead of an October 27 election, and analysts say his UNGA speech was aimed as much at people back home as it was at international viewers.
Dozens of envoys from around the world walked out as the speech began, some jeering and booing, while Netanyahu’s own team stood and applauded, and the speaker of the session shouted for order.
“If there are any other moral cowards who haven’t left this hall, please do so now,” Netanyahu said to those turning their backs on him.
He addressed the war that the US and Israel launched on Iran in February, saying: “Devastating Iran’s nuclear facilities was hard, was very hard to do.”
“But for me, it was one of the easiest decisions I’ve ever had to make as prime minister”, claiming that if he had not, “we’d all be dead”, he added.
In his own speech before the UNGA on Wednesday, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian also addressed the nuclear issue and called out the “double standard”.
“The nuclear weapon is in Israel, but the inspectors are in Iran. Israel kills, but Iran is subject to sanctions,” Pezeshkian said.
Netanyahu on Thursday said that Israel was fighting a “seven-front war”, including Gaza, the occupied West Bank, Syria, Lebanon, Iran, Yemen’s Houthis and militias in Iraq.
“We are going to win. We have no other choice,” Netanyahu declared, repeating the words of his older brother Yonatan Netanyahu, who was killed in 1976 during Operation Entebbe in Uganda.
In his speech, Netanyahu targeted Turkiye and its President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, among others, accusing Ankara of being a “spreader of anti-Semitic lies”.
The Turkish presidency responded with a statement saying that Netanyahu’s use of the UN platform to attack Erdogan was “incompatible with the ideals of peace, the rule of law and dialogue that the United Nations represents”. It pointed to the International Criminal Court’s arrest warrant against Netanyahu for war crimes and crimes against humanity.
“Netanyahu’s outrageous and despicable remarks targeting President Erdogan cannot obscure his massacres, the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza or the legal proceedings against him under international law,” Presidential Communications Director Burhanettin Duran said in a statement posted on X.
The Turkish president addressed the UNGA himself on Tuesday, saying Israel’s actions reflected a “genocidal mindset” and “state terrorism”, and that Gaza had become “the most inhumane and shameful concentration camp of our time”.
The United Kingdom and France, historic partners of Israel, were also in Netanyahu’s firing line. They have become increasingly outspoken in their criticism of the country’s actions and have both imposed limited sanctions on Israeli exports from the occupied West Bank.
“They accuse Israel, tiny Israel, of colonialism – some colonialism. And who’s accusing us? Among them are people in Britain and in France. For God’s sakes, they invented the term,” he said.
But Netanyahu thanked his “friend”, United States President Donald Trump.
“In this battle against the barbarians, we’ve had no greater partner than President Trump,” he said, as the US delegation joined the Israeli one in applauding Netanyahu’s remark.
“I thank him,” said Netanyahu, adding that Israel and the US had acted together as pilots from both countries “flew joint missions over the skies of Iran”.
Netanyahu said the US and Israel also “worked together to bring back our remaining hostages [from Gaza]”, as he defended Israeli actions in the enclave against charges of genocide.
“To all those spreading lies about my country, whether they sit in this hall or in the office of the anti-Semitic mayor of New York, I say this: shame on you,” Netanyahu said as he attacked Zohran Mamdani, who had previously said he would push for the arrest of the Israeli prime minister during his visit to the city.
“Mr Mamdani, you tried to stop me from coming here. You tried to silence me. Well, you can’t silence me,” Netanyahu said as he denied that Israel has committed genocide in Gaza.
Reacting to Netanyahu’s comments, Mamdani called the accusations against him “baseless lies” meant to “sanitise his genocide of Palestinians”.
Since October 7, 2023, Israel has faced repeated accusations of genocide in Gaza, as well as systematic war crimes in Gaza and the occupied West Bank.
The Hague-based International Criminal Court (ICC) said in 2024 it had reasonable grounds to believe Netanyahu was responsible for war crimes in Gaza, where over 73,000 Palestinians have been killed. Netanyahu denies the ICC charges.
Netanyahu attended the UNGA meeting despite an ICC warrant calling for his arrest. While he was welcomed, the Trump administration denied a visa for Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas, who addressed the UNGA through a prerecorded video statement from Ramallah earlier in the day.
As Netanyahu spoke, activists from US-based organisation Jewish Voice for Peace protested outside, accusing the United Nations of “playing host to a war criminal”.
“All across New York, Jews, Palestinians and people of conscience are rising up to demand an end to US support for the livestreamed horrors, rigged ceasefires and forever wars,” Sonya Meyerson-Knox, the group’s communications director, told Al Jazeera.
Meyerson-Knox said that “solidarity with Palestinian freedom has never been greater, and here in the US we are demanding with one voice to stop arming Israel”.
Adding to tensions, dozens of protesters, some brandishing “stop the genocide” banners, gathered near the UN. Several demonstrators were detained, including prominent actor Susan Sarandon.
Inside the UN, but addressing divisions back home in Israel, Netanyahu said: “Throughout this long war, our goal never wavers – to win with unwavering resolve … What unites us is so much stronger: our history, our values, our courage.”
Ariel Cohen, a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council’s Eurasia Center, said the Israeli prime minister delivered a “good speech” at the UNGA but that he did so in the “wrong forum”.
“That speech should be given at an election rally in Israel; this is who he’s communicating to,” Cohen told Al Jazeera. “He is making points that should be made to the Israeli audience for his political survival.”
Netanyahu is only making a whirlwind stop in New York before rushing back to Israel, where the election campaign is in full swing. He is not scheduled to meet any top US leaders.

Desperation begins early in an NFL season. A 0-3 start makes it nearly impossible to make the postseason, though the Houston Texans did so last season. Prior to the Texans, only six other teams in the modern era accomplished the same goal. Entering Week 3, eight teams faced the possibility of an 0-3 start, starting with the Atlanta Falcons on Thursday Night Football . The Falcons ensured they didn't find themselves in a hole they couldn't climb out of and may have found their starting QB along the way. For others, a season can be over much sooner than anyone expects.
Bleacher Report NFL analysts Brent Sobleski , Kris Knox , and Moe Moton will follow all of the action to break down each contest, provide takeaways and ask the most pressing questions.
Michael Penix Jr.'s Growing Confidence Provides Hope For Atlanta Falcons
The Atlanta Falcons already featured immense offensive talent at numerous spots. The quarterback position continued to hold back the team, though. Michael Penix Jr.s' performance Thursday against Green Bay Packers was quite promising after significant disappointment earlier in his career.
Penix started slowly during his first start after coming back from a torn ACL, including a poor interception on the opening drive where safety Xavier McKinney read the quarterback's eyes and easily drove on the pass for the turnover. From there, the 2024 eighth overall draft pick benefited greatly from Bijan Robinson running wild, offensive coordinator Tommy Rees giving the quarterback simple reasons and plenty of quick-hitters and manufactured touches to build the 26-year-old's confidence.
By the end of the game, Penix finished the contest with 256 passing and a touchdown. He also completed 72 percent of his passes.
The quarterback's performance is exactly what Atlanta needed to try and build something positive. It's a significant turn of events considering the Falcons wanted to enter this season with Tua Tagovailoa as their QB1.
Spoiler Alert: Bijan Robinson Continues to Run Wild
Robinson is arguably the game's best running back. The Packers won't argue after Thursday's performance.
Green Bay knew it had to slow the Falcons' lead back and failed spectacularly when trying to do so. Robinson's 29 carries became a new career-high, while he finished two short of doing the same with 194 rushing yards.
The 24-year-old ball-carrier sliced through Green Bay's defense, scored twice and served as a big-play threat even though Penix wasn't comfortable early and the Packers could key on Atlanta's run game—which showed how dynamic he really is.
Can Green Bay Do Anything To Improve Its Run Game? The Packers entered Thursday's contest with the league's worst rushing offense. Green Bay's latest performance only made matters worse. Matt LaFleur's unit had been averaging 64.5 rushing yards per game. The Packers managed a measly 17 yards against the Falcons. MarShawn Lloyd led the team. He produced 11 yards on four carries. With Josh Jacobs' on the commissioner's exempt list with a potential league suspension forthcoming, general manager Brian Gutekunst must look at alternatives. Remaining free agents aren't promising. A potential trade could happen. The New Orleans Saints' Alvin Kamara may be the biggest name on the trade block. Of course, the offensive line could help matters, but that doesn't seem likely. Packers' O-Line Is Making Life Miserable for QB Jordan Love Four-fifths of Green Bay's front five is unproven and it shows. Jacob Monk moved from center to right guard, and he's a full-time starter for the first time in the NFL career. Anthony Belton took over at right tackle after Zach Bako-Bewele suffered a season-ending knee injury. Rookie Jager Burton moved into left guard for the injured Aaron Banks. Plus, Jordan Morgan may be a former first-round pick, but this season is his first as the squad's left tackle. As a result, Green Bay can't run the ball, and Love isn't comfortable in the pocket. While the Falcons sacked Love only once, Atlanta hit him on 12 different occasions and applied consistent pressure. An offense can't do much if its offensive line isn't solid, and Green Bay is a prime example.

articles.title_orig: Mikey Musumeci slammed hard at UFC BJJ but ultimately wins decision over Bryce Mitchell in main event
articles.title_zh: Mikey Musumeci slammed hard at UFC BJJ but ultimately wins decision over Bryce Mitchell in main event
articles.content_orig:
Mikey Musumeci had to endure a huge slam from Bryce Mitchell before winning a decision on Thursday
Mikey Musumeci came close on several submissions but the UFC BJJ champion was unable to put Bryce Mitchell away in their three round main event on Thursday night in Las Vegas.
The crossover match was set up as Musumeci has started to make his transition to a full-time MMA fighter and he showed off his skills without using any leg locks, which is one of his signature moves. Mitchell defended effectively over three rounds and despite not getting the finish, Musumeci had the time of his life.
“It was fun,” Musumechi said after the match. “I like that. I’m training MMA now so I like that. I want more MMA grappling opponents. I would prefer to do this style of grappling. It was way more fun for me.”
It took Musumeci just a moment to pull guard and he started pulling for leg locks, which got a few boos from the crowd after the competitors agreed on no leg locks. Musumeci did release the early hold. Musumeci again grabbed onto the leg as he went for the sweep and he quickly transitioned to an anaconda choke and then a power guillotine choke.
To his credit, Mitchell did a good job resisting the submission and eventually breaking free from the submission attempt.
On the restart in round two, Mitchell was able to get on top with Musumeci looking for an omo plata from the bottom. Musumeci stayed on his back trying to grab onto the arm or the head but Mitchell defended effectively as the match moved into the third and final round.
With Musumeci in guard, Mitchell was grinding his forehead into his opponent and then out of nowhere, the UFC bantamweight executed a huge slam that earned him a warning from referee Vitor Ribeiro.
This time, Musumeci executed a slick takedown of his own as he tried to set up a submission after taking the back. Musumeci had Mitchell in trouble after grabbing an arm but “Thug Nasty” stayed calm and composed to avoid the submission.
Mitchell bull rushed forward with another takedown before the match ended but to his credit, the UFC bantamweight held his own against one of the top grapplers in the world. Afterwards, Mitchell admitted he’d have to use punches to escape many of Musumeci’s best moves but they stuck to their agreement for the fight that ultimately lasted all 15 minutes.
There’s no word yet when Musumeci might actually take his first MMA fight now that he’s training full time at Syndicate MMA in Las Vegas but Thursday’s match proved that “Darth Rigatoni” is that much closer to his first official fight.

Rep. Claudia Tenney, R-N.Y., discusses President Donald Trump’s prediction that the Iran war will end after the 2026 midterm elections on ‘Fox Report.’
Despite voter fury and rising fuel prices, most Republican senators stayed the course with President Donald Trump and his war on Iran in a vote Thursday.
Though vulnerable Republicans on the campaign trail broke with Trump earlier this week, calling for an "immediate end" to the war, lawmakers on the Hill stuck with him and defeated another attempt by Democrats to rein in his war authorities as the conflict nears the eight-month mark.
Still, there was a group of rebellious Republicans who had consistently voted with Democrats, including Sens. Susan Collins, R-Maine, Lisa Murkowski, R-Alaska, Rand Paul, R-Ky. New blood was added this time with Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C.
REPUBLICANS BREAK WITH TRUMP TO REBUKE IRAN WAR — BUT IT WON'T CHANGE POLICY
President Donald Trump during the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Sept. 22, 2026. (Bloomberg via Getty Images)
Tillis, who is retiring at the end of the year, argued his decision to vote for the latest war powers resolution came after the administration again blew past a 60-day deadline to involve Congress.
"We know the resolution's not gonna pass, but it is important to start saying, ‘We deserve an update. You better start treating — Congress can be an assistance with this war effort, if you inform us,’" Tillis said.
To Tillis’ point, the resolution that failed in the Senate, which passed in the House with seven Republican defectors, would have headed to the president’s desk, where it likely would have been vetoed. And without a veto-proof majority, the effort wouldn't have teeth legally. However, it will hurt on the airwaves in the ads to come.
GOP CRACKS WIDEN OVER IRAN WAR AS VULNERABLE CANDIDATES BREAK WITH TRUMP, DEMAND ITS END
Thursday’s vote comes as Republicans are getting an earful about the war, particularly over skyrocketing gas and diesel prices, on the campaign trail. Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., acknowledged that fuel prices are a growing issue for Americans.
"Well, I think people are, there's voter fatigue with high gas prices and high diesel prices in my part of the world," Thune said.
"So, that's a frustration, it's an economic frustration, and that's why, again, I hope the administration is laser-focused on trying to get the [Strait of Hormuz] open, get the shipping lights opened up, and help out with that global energy supply, because that ultimately will get prices down," he continued.
Three vulnerable Republicans running for toss-up seats this week, Rep. Ashley Hinson, R-Iowa, former Rep. Mike Rogers in Michigan, and Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, all requested that the fighting come to an "immediate end" as the war grows in unpopularity with their voters.
TRUMP DEFENDS US INTERVENTIONS ABROAD AHEAD OF 'BIG DECISION' ON IRAN: 'SETTLING YEARS OF UNFINISHED BUSINESS'
Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., plans to force a vote on his war powers resolution to rein in President Donald Trump's military action in Iran. (Graeme Sloan/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., who has acted as the self-anointed traffic cop for the deluge of Democratic war powers resolutions over the last several months, diagnosed the defections as a by-product of reports that U.S. bombs had fallen on an Iranian school and that diesel costs are "going up and up and up."
"They are listening to their constituents. They should [have] listened to them before now, because their constituents were saying, ‘Don't get into this thing,’" Kaine said. "But they're finally listening to them. And nothing makes you listen as much as an election staring you in the face."

But Trump isn’t swayed by the effects that the conflict could have on the midterm elections as the GOP fights to keep power in Congress.
"The Republican Party is running, and I'll be helping them, but I am not running," Trump told reporters this week. "I gave absolutely no credence and will not give credence to the election when it comes to Iran. It doesn't even enter my mind. The only thing that does is that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon."

articles.title_orig: Media outlets banned by Trump denied access to White House dinner despite judge's order
articles.title_zh: Media outlets banned by Trump denied access to White House dinner despite judge's order
articles.content_orig:
CNN and MS NOW reporters say they have been denied entry to cover a White House state dinner despite a judge ruling their access to the grounds must be restored.
A federal judge said in an overnight ruling that the White House ban on three outlets - CNN and MS NOW and Politico - was likely unconstitutional and that the administration must allow them access, for now. Trump barred them last week, accusing them of "fake news".
Journalists with the three outlets were allowed back in on Thursday morning.
Then in the evening, a CNN reporter and a producer and an MS NOW reporter said that they were denied entry to cover the guests arriving for a state dinner for Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
The outlets said they had properly submitted their reporters' names for credentials to cover the arrivals.
CNN said that about an hour before Xi was scheduled to arrive, the White House said it could cover the event only with a photojournalist and audio technician, but not a team that included a reporter and producer.
MS NOW White House reporter Laura Barron-Lopez said she was told by White House staff that she could not be let in, and to contact the White House communications director.
The BBC has contacted the White House for comment.
A White House communications account posted on X that "contrary to what the Fake News wants you to believe, they don't just get to have free rein into every part of the White House, every event, and every press call".
The incident was the latest in a series of events on Thursday surrounding the ban on some media outlets at the White House.
Despite the overnight ruling, CNN, Politico and MS NOW all reported being denied entry to the White House on Thursday morning, prompting a request for an emergency court hearing.
In response, the director of White House Operations said in a court filing that the press passes and confiscated badges had been restored by 09:45 local time (13:45 GMT).
Shortly afterwards, all three outlets said they were allowed back in.
However, networks including Fox News, NBC, CBS and ABC, which pulled out in solidarity, have yet to confirm they will resume broadcast coverage from the White House.
The chaotic standoff limited some TV coverage as Trump welcomed Xi to the White House ahead of a state dinner.
In his ruling, Judge Timothy Kelly said the ban on the outlets should be temporarily lifted because it "likely violated their constitutional due process rights".
He cast doubt on White House claims that the ban was justified in part on national security grounds, pointing out the president made no mention of this in his initial announcement.
"The record lacks factual support for defendants' contention that the revocation of plaintiffs' hard passes will in fact protect national security," Kelly wrote.
Judge Kelly ruled CNN, Politico and MS NOW were "likely to succeed" in showing the White House had not exercised "adequate due process" in the ban.
He ordered the immediate return of the outlets' press passes and a halt to enforcement of the ban for 14 days.
In a court filing on Tuesday, the US Department of Justice had accused the news outlets of threatening national security with their coverage.
Government lawyers cited stories about missile stockpiles, the construction of the White House ballroom and the recent Republican midterm convention.
Trump first announced last Friday he was barring the three outlets from the White House, accusing them of writing "fiction or lies" about his administration.
By Saturday morning, each outlet reported that they were denied entry to t he White House grounds and that their press badges were confiscated.
All three outlets accused the Trump administration of violating their constitutional rights.
In a joint statement on Monday, they said they were pursuing legal action to "defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports".
More than 50 media organisations across the ideological spectrum filed an amicus brief in support of the lawsuit, including Fox News, the New York Times, the Washington Post and the Wall Street Journal.
There have been previous instances of administrations attempting to limit certain outlets' access.
The Obama administration tried to exclude Fox News from participating in a specific press pool interview with an administration official in 2009.
But after objections from the other four networks in the press pool, Fox News was allowed in.

articles.title_zh: Unused Tents and Uneaten Food: Watchdog Finds ‘Waste’ in Immigration Crackdown
articles.content_orig:
In a single day in January, Immigration and Customs Enforcement spent more money than it had on any other day in either of President Trump's terms, federal spending records show.
The agency advanced billions to Chicago Title Insurance in escrow to acquire detention facilities, according to a Department of Homeland Security spokesperson. Over the next two months, ICE used $1.07 billion of the funds to purchase 11 warehouses it planned to convert to detention megacenters, seven of which the agency now plans to sell.
The rest of the money sat with the firm for months after ICE abandoned the warehouse plan. In July and August, ICE moved $2.2 billion from Chicago Title to purchase four detention facilities from CoreCivic, a private prison company it separately pays to continue operating them.
In its rush to expand detention capacity, ICE wasted millions of taxpayer dollars, the Government Accountability Office found in a report released Thursday. The agency failed to account for long-term costs in acquiring detention centers and lost $20 million in unrecoverable costs purchasing the warehouses it no longer plans to use, the review found. Even more could be lost if ICE sells the warehouses for less than what it paid for them, the GAO report said.
Barring any undisclosed purchases, $1.55 billion still sits with Chicago Title Insurance for acquiring detention centers as ICE continues its push to double the number of detention beds in service of the president's mass deportation agenda. Just this week, ICE awarded several companies contracts that could reach a combined $10 billion to expand and construct new facilities.
GAO concluded that "urgent planning" is necessary to reduce further waste. ICE said it would produce a strategic plan by Aug. 31, 2027, a date the watchdog said wasn't soon enough.
"We just saw a real lack of planning overall," said Heather MacLeod, director of Homeland Security and Justice at GAO. "The lack of planning has really led to stops and starts which have ultimately resulted in waste."
GAO's report did not estimate a total amount potentially lost to waste, but MacLeod said another review of ICE spending is currently underway.
Flush with cash after Congress funneled $75 billion to the agency — including $45 billion to expand detention capacity — through President Trump's " One Big Beautiful Bill Act ," ICE has nearly doubled its spending this year. The agency spent $19 billion from last October to July, the most recent month for which data is available, up from $11 billion the previous full fiscal year, a CBS News analysis of federal data found.
A DHS spokesperson wrote to CBS News that ICE is "working at turbo speed on cost-effective and innovative ways to deliver on the American people's mandate for mass deportations of criminal illegal aliens," and that the spending bill known as OBBBA has provided "historic funding" to help it carry out the mandate.
Appropriating funds outside of the typical process — and without the usual guardrails that come in appropriations bills — means ICE has more flexibility in how it can use the funding, said Kevin McNellis, a policy and budget analyst who previously worked in the Congressional Budget Office and Congressional Research Service. That also leads to a breakdown in oversight, he wrote in a report he authored for Co-Equal, a nonprofit focused on congressional authority.
"When DHS only had annual funding or relied on the annual appropriations for the majority of its funding, there were long standing systems and processes in place for DHS to inform Congress of its spending plan and for Congress to then oversee those spending plans," McNellis told CBS News. "The situation we've been in since OBBBA passed is we have an unprecedented amount of money, appropriated outside those long-standing processes, trying to be spent very quickly."
ICE paid an 11% to 13% premium on the 11 warehouses it purchased, according to CoStar, a real estate analytics firm. Former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem directed ICE to purchase new detention sites within 30 days, contributing to the high prices, The Wall Street Journal reported .
The remaining warehouses ICE still hopes to convert face legal challenges, though ICE already signed contracts worth a combined $426 million to renovate two of them. No detainees are currently held in any of the warehouses.
After dropping the warehouse plan, ICE spent $1.47 billion purchasing two California detention facilities from CoreCivic in July. The next month, ICE bought another two CoreCivic facilities in Kansas and Minnesota for a combined $734 million. In its announcement of the August purchases, CoreCivic said the company is in talks with ICE to sell more facilities.
CoreCivic is using the profits from the sales to pay down its debts, according to company filings .
GAO found that ICE had only forecasted costs for these centers and to-be-converted warehouses for the next three years, failing to consider how it would pay for them once the funds Congress has allocated through 2029 run out.
The watchdog also found that through FEMA reimbursements, ICE paid the state of Florida almost triple its typical per-bed rate for two state-operated facilities, including the now-shuttered facility dubbed "Alligator Alcatraz." ICE skipped typical contract negotiation practices, creating a new grant program with the state of Florida as the only eligible recipient, according to the GAO report. FEMA paid Florida a total of $608.4 million for "Alligator Alcatraz," GAO said.
ICE is also paying more than it typically would per-bed to house noncitizen detainees at facilities operated by the Bureau of Prisons. BOP officials told GAO they've had to pay staff overtime and for temporary assignments to meet ICE's needs, resulting in a per-bed-rate double that of ICE's median rate.
Another abandoned initiative GAO cited was ICE's efforts to launch detention facilities at military bases, like the one at Camp East Montana in El Paso. A previous GAO review found ICE spent $7.1 million on detainee meals it did not need at the El Paso facility. ICE dropped its plan to launch similar facilities on military installations in Indiana and New Jersey, GAO reported.
ICE also spent $2.85 million on tents at Guantanamo Bay to house detainees that were never used. The facility, initially planned for 30,000 detainees, held only a handful. In May, CBS News reported that the Guantanamo Bay facility was holding just six detainees. The agency is still trying to house detainees on the naval base: this week it signed a contract with the same company it used to help procure the warehouses and acquire the CoreCivic facilities to construct a facility at Guantanamo Bay and at other sites.
DHS's Inspector General is conducting its own audit into ICE's acquisition of detention space to determine whether it made purchases in a "cost-effective manner." The internal watchdog is also probing ICE spending on air charter services and its reporting on how it is using Big Beautiful Bill funds.
"We think it's important that DHS and ICE do develop a plan going forward tied to their needs and what they're trying to get out of their expansion efforts," she said. "We're encouraged to see that they agreed with our recommendation and we're hoping they'll take steps to address it quickly."

articles.title_orig: U.S. Intercedes for Elon Musk’s X Over European Fine
articles.title_zh: U.S. Intercedes for Elon Musk’s X Over European Fine
articles.content_orig:
The US government is seeking to join Elon Musk's legal challenge to overturn a €120m (£105m) EU fine against X over its blue tick badges.
In December 2025, the European Commission said the platform "deceives users" by allowing people to pay for a blue verified check mark, because it is not "meaningfully verifying" who is behind the account.
But US Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate said on Thursday that the commission had "inappropriately attempted" to expand its reach to American companies outside its control.
Musk, who spent millions helping elect Donald Trump and other Republicans, has previously claimed EU tech regulation "inhibits progress" for companies.
The US Department of Justice (DOJ) has filed an application with the EU's General Court in support of Musk's and X's attempts to dismiss ​the case.
It claims that under a section of law in the Statute of the Court of Justice of the EU, a state may intervene in disputes before the court if it "can establish an interest in the result of the case to the court".
The DOJ said the US "has a clear interest" in ensuring any decision by the commission was applied consistently with "how territorial jurisdiction is generally understood in international law".
It also wants to make sure it would not "otherwise prejudice" US-headquartered digital services that "contribute significantly" to its economy.
In a press briefing on Friday , European Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier said it was "ready to defend" its position in court.
He added that the commission had an "solid case" at its disposal, due to the alleged breach of its Digital Services Act.
In addition to its use of blue ticks, EU regulators had accused X of failing to provide transparency around its adverts and denying researchers access to public data.
Henna Virkkunen, the regulator's executive vice-president for tech sovereignty, said at the time of the fine's issue it was "holding X responsible for undermining users' rights and evading accountability".
"Deceiving users with blue checkmarks, obscuring information on ads and shutting out researchers have no place online in the EU," she said.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) had criticised the EU regulator, accusing it of attacking and censoring US firms.
"The European Commission's fine isn't just an attack on X, it's an attack on all American tech platforms and the American people by foreign governments," Rubio wrote in a post on X.
"The days of censoring Americans online are over."
His remarks were reposted by Musk, who added "absolutely".
The European Commission denied targeting any specific nationality, stating it is simply protecting its digital and democratic standards to maintain its role as a global benchmark.
The action marked the Commission's first official non-compliance decision under the Digital Services Act (DSA), one of two mandatory rulebooks governing online platforms in the EU.
However, the EU is also conducting several other investigations into the platform, including one into its integrated AI assistant Grok over concerns it was used to create sexualised images of real people.

articles.title_orig: Bond yields surge to fresh two-decade highs, but oil prices are buffeted by Iran headlines
articles.title_zh: Bond yields surge to fresh two-decade highs, but oil prices are buffeted by Iran headlines
articles.content_orig:
Morning Rundown: Key takeaways from the Trump-Xi summit, Bill Gates wants AI oversight, and what to know about measles in newborns
Key U.S. Treasury yields surged to fresh two-decade highs Thursday as the price of oil jumped to as high as $108 per barrel.
The yield on the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond soared as high as 5.47%, a level not seen in 22 years.
After having posted its biggest one-day rise since April 2025, the yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury bond continued advancing Thursday. In early trading, it climbed as high as 5.18%. That remains its highest since 2007.
Because of the influence the 10-year yield has over consumer borrowing rates, the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate jumped to 7.37% on Thursday, its highest since May 2024.
Meanwhile, oil prices jumped again overnight after a mediated U.S. dialogue with Iran at the United Nations General Assembly produced no tangible evidence of any progress toward ending the seven-month war.
Much of the day’s gains in oil were reversed shortly after midday ET after Reuters reported that U.S. and Iranian negotiators are exploring a phased path out of the war. The path reportedly involves Tehran’s reopening the Strait of Hormuz, according to Reuters’ multiple unnamed sources .
NBC News has not confirmed the Reuters report.
The reversal was short-lived, however, and international Brent crude oil continued to rise and closed higher by 3.4%, at $106.60. U.S. crude oil ended the day higher by 2.6%, at $94.61 per barrel.
Since the start of the year, both Brent and West Texas Intermediary crude are up more than 65%.
The rising oil prices have continued to push commercial diesel fuel prices to records. On Thursday, the national average price for diesel was $6.51, effectively unchanged from a day earlier but up 73% since the Iran war began.
Likewise, the national average price of regular unleaded gas was 50% higher Thursday than it was when the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran in late February, at $4.48 per gallon.
Stocks fell in early trading, but like oil, they sharply reversed course on the Reuters report. The S&P 500 erased a drop of 0.5%, while the Nasdaq Composite erased a 0.9% slip. Both indexes closed flat.
Around the world, the bond sell-off is roiling sovereign debt markets.
“The acceleration higher in US rates yesterday is being felt globally as to highlight for the umpteenth time that we’re all in this global bond boat together,” wrote Peter Boockvar, chief investment officer at OnePoint BFG Wealth.
The yield on Japan’s 10-year bond rose to its highest level since 1996 on Thursday, while Germany’s 10-year bund notched its highest yield since 2009.
“As summer officially ends, macro data are still fairly solid in the US, as indicated by a 4%-type unemployment rate and 2%-ish growth,” wrote Bank of America’s global rates analysts.
“But the risks continue to pile up for anxious markets,” they added, pointing to ongoing trade wars, the energy supply shock, upcoming midterm elections and potential risks to the AI boom.
A major driver of the surge in bond yields this week was a report from S&P Global, released Wednesday morning, that found that while U.S. business activity accelerated in September, “firms’ input costs have meanwhile jumped in September at the steepest rate for four years, with fuel and transport costs spiking higher.”
That led investors and traders to ramp up their bets on Fed rate hikes.
Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams said the central bank still has more work to do to help bring down inflation.
It’s “likely that another rate hike may be appropriate by the end of the year,” Williams said Thursday in a speech in London.
Nonetheless, he said, the U.S. economy has demonstrated “remarkable resilience” in the face of “significant shocks” hitting it.
Another key official, Anna Paulson, president of the Philadelphia Fed, said Thursday that she, too, expects “some modest further tightening may be warranted.”
In central banker parlance, tightening refers to raising rates.
The rise in bond yields has continued despite a series of measures taken — and warnings delivered — by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent this month.
“ I am the house now ,” Bessent said Sept. 8, “and you can bet against me if you want.”
At the time, Bessent was defending a Treasury Department intervention to help prop up the Japanese yen. The hope was that a stronger yen would relieve pressure on the Japanese government to sell U.S. Treasury bonds.
But it hasn’t entirely worked, and as of Thursday, the yen had again weakened to levels on par with its exchange rate against the U.S. dollar from early September.
Bessent has also intervened in the U.S. bond markets, buying back longer-dated Treasurys in an effort to keep their yields low.
In response to the department’s initial buyback this month, bond yields rose — exactly the opposite reaction from what the administration intended.
Bessent has brushed off the stumble, insisting that the U.S. bond market is still the “best performing” in the world and crediting President Donald Trump for it.
“If some of the Bloomberg Terminal bros are unhappy with what I’m doing, well, that’s too bad,” Bessent said in an interview Sept. 10.
The second round of Bessent’s buyback plan was conducted Thursday, when the Treasury bought back about $4 billion worth of 20- and 30-year bonds. As with the initial round, yields rose to their highest level of the session on the news — but the jump was far less notable than it had been a month ago.
“Mechanically, today’s operation went more smoothly,” said Brian Rehling, co-head of global fixed-income strategy at Wells Fargo. But “long-end yields are still being set by inflation, Fed expectations” and the volume of debt being issued.
“Today’s operation is unlikely to alter the trajectory of long-term interest rates, which we believe will continue to move higher until the market believes inflation is being brought under control,” he added.
“US Treasury Secretary ‘House’ Bessent seems to be demonstrating the house does not always win,” Paul Donovan, the chief economist at UBS Global Wealth Management, wrote Thursday morning.
CORRECTION (Sept. 24, 2026, 2:19 p.m. ET): A previous version of this article misstated Thursday’s national average price for diesel. It was $6.51, not $4.51.
Steve Kopack is a senior reporter at NBC News covering business and the economy.

Ole Miss junior Robert Strang, 20, was found dead alongside retail packages of kratom, according to Mississippi investigators.
Authorities also found freshman Aidan Hamilton dead in a separate location with similar packages.
Strang's family, who released a photo Thursday evening, said in a statement that they are trying to process an "unimaginable loss."
Officials have not yet determined the official cause of death for either student.
Investigators are currently awaiting toxicology report results to confirm whether kratom played a role.
Kratom comes from a tree in Southeast Asia and acts like an opioid in the human body.
While it remains legal for anyone 21 and older in Georgia, Dean Francis of End Kratom Addiction warned that users often take increasing amounts just to feel normal.
Rob Hauser with Georgia Sky Outpatient Detox, which operates in Acworth and Marietta, noted that kratom addiction now overtakes fentanyl withdrawal cases in some instances.
Georgia lawmakers proposed a bill in January to completely ban kratom , but the measure failed to reach the governor's desk.
The supplement is available in smoke shops, gas stations and convenience stores, and remains legal in all but eight states.
According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, kratom use has surged 2,500% over the last decade.

In 2024, Microsoft and Qualcomm kicked off a new category of Windows hardware it called "Copilot+ PCs" that set the baseline for a new wave of AI-first computers, and launched with exclusive features that would not be made available on PCs that didn't meet a new set of system requirements.
The launch didn't go smoothly. Copilot+ PCs were met with immediate backlash from security researchers after discovering that Copilot+ PCs blockbuster feature, Recall, was woefully insecure. This forced the company to delay Recall and ship this new category of devices without its leading AI experience.
This pretty much tarnished the Copilot+ PC brand, and over the last two years more and more OEMs have dropped the moniker from marketing materials and product names. In fact, even Microsoft has seemingly stopped mentioning it.
I've noticed that none of the Surface PCs launched in 2026 include the Copilot+ PC moniker in their product names, unlike the Surface PCs that launched in 2025 and before. Now, you have to go digging to find any mention of Copilot+ compatibility in specification sheets.
At this year's Snapdragon Summit, I had the chance to ask Surface CVP Brett Ostrum about the lack of Copilot+ PC branding on its recent Surface PCs , and he confirmed that " these are not called Copilot+ PCs. They do meet all the requirements of our previous bar for what Copilot+ devices are. We still lean into the narrative around AI on the edge and being able to have a hybrid solution out there."
I've also asked Qualcomm's SVP of compute, Kedar Kondap, about his thoughts on the usage of the Copilot+ PC branding. He told me that "the purpose for Copilot+ PCs was to be able to deliver [NPU] experiences. So it was to define a certain category of devices with a certain bar and metric, like for example, a 45 TOPS NPU ... So from that perspective, it's more offering the same experiences, probably without just using [Copilot+ PC] terminology now. "
It's also worth mentioning that NVIDIA hasn't gone anywhere near the Copilot+ PC brand for its upcoming RTX Spark platform, even though all RTX Spark PCs meet the Copilot+ PC specification bar. I suspect that's a deliberate decision.
It seems pretty obvious that the Copilot+ PC brand hasn't resonated with the market, and OEMs and Microsoft itself are now quietly pulling back on that branding. The specification baseline for Copilot+ PC experiences still exists, it just no longer has a pretty marketing name tied to it.
The rough launch of Copilot+ PCs, paired with the fact that Microsoft Copilot itself doesn't have a very strong reputation these days, likely contributed to the decision to slowly retire the Copilot+ PC branding. The brand never made sense to me anyway... these PCs have nothing to do with Copilot.
